page: UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-960GB-4xH100 is a GPU-accelerated server configured with 48 physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The system features 960.0 GB of system memory, providing 20.0 GB per core. Acceleration is driven by four NVIDIA H100 GPUs from the Hopper architecture, delivering a combined 320 GB of VRAM. This server operates on the KVM hypervisor and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Notably, local storage is not bundled with this instance type, and the CPU allocation is designated as shared.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, achieving a stress-ng multi-core score of 96,293.69 and a PassMark CPU score of 85,426.66. Memory performance is highlighted by a top-tier small-block read bandwidth of 7,649.82 GB/sec, alongside a strong large-block read bandwidth of 316.04 GB/sec. Cryptographic and vector processing are supported by hardware flags such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX, reflected in a top-tier PassMark extended instructions score of 117,918.35. For language model workloads, prompt processing for a 135M model reaches 10,308.98 tokens/sec, while text generation registers at 377.14 tokens/sec.

The hardware profile presents specific architectural tradeoffs. While the system offers massive GPU and system memory resources, the CPU allocation is shared, and there is no integrated local storage, requiring external storage attachments. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of GPU and memory resources relative to the CPU core count makes it structured for specialized parallel processing rather than general-purpose compute. This configuration is suited for large-scale machine learning, LLM inference, parallelized data decompression, and cryptographic processing.

Operating on the KVM hypervisor with an x86_64 architecture, this instance utilizes a shared CPU allocation and contains no local storage. Given the lack of local storage and the shared CPU model, this server is designed for workloads requiring massive GPU acceleration and high memory capacity, such as machine learning inference, deep learning training, and complex parallel computations.
